claim: For a delta-hedged long straddle, the P&L over a short interval is approximately one-half gamma times S squared times (realized variance minus implied variance) times dt, so the position profits only if realized volatility exceeds the implied volatility paid; the ATM straddle's daily break-even move is about S times IV divided by the square root of 252.

evidence.quote: dP&L ≈ ½ Γ S² (σ² realized − σ² implied ) dt

claim: A long strangle has positive vega, decays faster than a comparable straddle, has break-evens further apart, and has a greater chance of losing 100% at expiration (Fidelity).

evidence.quote: When volatility falls, long straddles decrease in price and lose money.
Thus, when there is little or no stock price movement, a long strangle will experience a greater percentage loss over a given time period than a comparable straddle.
